title: Transformers and Rectifiers (India) Limited (TARIL): Business, Valuation and Portfolio Action
primer: TARIL builds high-voltage power transformers with a ₹7,237 Cr Q2 FY27 backlog, yet FY26 CFO was negative ₹105.38 Cr and H1 borrowings jumped 27% to ₹581 Cr. Pass 1 also uncovered World Bank Sanctions Case No. 788, two rapid external CEO exits, and DII ownership falling from 7.68% to 1.19%. Both the 2026-11-23 NSE close (₹289.45) and 2026-11-25 live TradingView close (₹287.95) breached the ₹292.47 stop in STAGE_4. New capital is REJECTED (TIER_0); EXIT_IMMEDIATELY all 150 Zerodha shares (1.02% weight) and redeploy 60% to cash and 40% to Stage 2 shortlist compounder GRWRHITECH.
entry_posture: AVOID_STAGE4_OR_BROKEN; Stage 4 breakdown below ₹292.47 stop with negative probability-weighted expected return
holding_rationale: Exit all 150 Zerodha shares immediately (avg cost ₹309.42; cost basis ₹46,413.31; 2026-11-23 NSE ledger value ₹43,417.50 / -6.45%; 2026-11-25 live TradingView value ₹43,192.50 / -6.94%; 1.02% portfolio weight). Both closes decisively breached the prior ₹292.47 structural stop inside a STAGE_4 breakdown (CAP_REJECTED) while Pass 1 surfaced World Bank Sanctions Case No. 788, dual external CEO exits, DII attrition to 1.19%, and a 27% H1 FY27 borrowings surge to ₹581 Cr. Per the upward-only stop ratchet, ₹292.47 is never lowered. This is an advisory instruction, not an automated broker order.

destinations.rationale: On the 2026-11-25 live TradingView snapshot, CGPOWER (₹778.90, 89.26x P/E) and VOLTAMP (₹9,676.00, 30.88x P/E) are both in Stage 4 breakdown (CAP_REJECTED), while POWERINDIA (₹29,770.00, 110.16x P/E) sits in Stage 1 basing at a triple-digit multiple.
